title: Natural Language Explainable Recommendation with Robustness Enhancement

problem.claim: Natural language explainable recommendation should generate explanations for similar user-item pairs that are not too different.

gap.claim: Previous models mostly focus on explanation accuracy, while robustness has been largely ignored.

contributions.claim: The work formulates robust natural language explainable recommendation as a recommendation problem.
The work designs four heuristic methods that modify adversarial outputs using weighted token probabilities and synonym replacements.
The work designs a dual-policy reinforcement learning framework that models language generation as a decision-making problem to improve robustness.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that robust natural language explainable recommendation is addressed for the first time in this field.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments demonstrating the effectiveness of their framework.

narrative_sequence.summary: Natural language explainable recommendation is presented as a promising direction for more efficient and informed user decisions.
Prior work emphasizes explanation accuracy, but robustness has been largely overlooked.
Robustness requires accounting for differing token importance and judging output similarity through continuous token semantics.
The work formulates robust explainable recommendation and combines heuristic adversarial-output modification with dual-policy reinforcement learning.
The authors report extensive experiments supporting the effectiveness of the framework.

source_observation.claim: The abstract identifies token importance and continuous token semantics as distinct characteristics of robustness in natural language generation.

interpretation.claim: Robustness objectives for generated language may need to distinguish token roles and semantic similarity rather than rely only on token-level overlap.

application.claim: When designing robustness methods for generated text, consider weighted token-level perturbations together with semantic comparisons.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that these design choices generalize beyond the described recommendation setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or quantitative experimental results.
The abstract does not describe the four heuristic methods individually or provide implementation details for the reinforcement learning framework.
